title: Daemon Supervisor: Deterministic Event Loops, Ephemeral Agent Dispatch & Operational Rails
target_platform: Host daemon (macOS first; Python asyncio prototype, Rust port optional) supervising ephemeral local headless CLI agents (claude -p, cursor-agent, repo CLIs); pluggable secondary remote/cloud worker (e.g. Grok Bot, webhooks) for browser or out-of-band tasks
hypothesis: A zero-token, event-driven supervisor daemon can reliably orchestrate multi-step agent lifecycles, handle sequential state changes, and enforce operational rails (process timeouts, budget trips, state rollback) without burning tokens during idle state monitoring.
falsification_criteria: The daemon fails to detect status transitions on disk within 2 seconds, allows an agent process to exceed hard timeout boundaries without SIGKILL termination, or requires model inference to maintain the listening event loop. Case counts and the measurement protocol are to be frozen before the confirmatory test.

model_routing.cli_target: local headless CLI (claude -p / cursor-agent / repo CLI); optional remote worker
model_routing.routing_guidance: Outer loop is deterministic; models run only inside dispatched ephemeral runs, each under its own budget.

evidence.details: Amended confirmatory run 2 (freeze_v2.json, 800a9bc9f): C1 20/20 detections, max 0.014 s (<2 s); C2 5/5 TIMED_OUT at 2.12-2.13 s with process group gone; C3 15 s idle, 0 dispatches, 0.07% CPU; C4 circuit opened after 3 failures, held, resumed after reset; C5 ordered, 0 bad reads; C6 4/4 gated jobs REJECTED; C7 recovered on attempt 2. Run 1 (00a0cda4d) failed C2 from a test-design defect (circuit breaker held trials 4-5); disclosed amendment. Live demo: real Haiku job via cli-agent plus a verified commit job.

lessons_learned: On macOS, killpg(pgid, 0) raises EPERM when only a zombie group leader remains; reap the leader inside the kill loop.
cli-agent run_agent.py adds --dangerously-skip-permissions for claude/agy unless --isolated; a dispatcher must pass --isolated and gate any bypass explicitly.
Tests of one rail must isolate it from other rails: five consecutive timeouts correctly tripped the 3-failure circuit breaker.

resources: local CPU; no idle model calls

experiment: 1) Inventory existing capabilities first (cli-agent launch controls --timeout/--claim-dir/--result-json, manage_coordination.py leases, Agentic OS control plane) and reuse them. 2) Scaffold the daemon in LEARNING/experiments/mission-001/daemon/: OS-event file watcher (kqueue via watchfiles/watchdog, polling fallback with backoff); daemon state machine STAGED->QUEUED->RUNNING->COMPLETED|FAILED|BLOCKED_ON_HUMAN with atomic writes (temp file + os.replace); isolated subprocess runner with max_wall_clock_seconds (SIGTERM then SIGKILL), max_consecutive_failures (-> BLOCKED_ON_HUMAN), per-run run.log; abstract runner interface (local CLI, container, remote webhook). 3) Tests: detects QUEUED->RUNNING; kills a hanging `sleep 60`; records non-zero exit traces. Evidence in LEARNING/experiments/mission-001/evidence/.
design_constraints: Daemon states (QUEUED, RUNNING, BLOCKED_ON_HUMAN, ...) live in the daemon's own state file; mission manifests keep schema statuses only (PROPOSED/STAGED/IN_PROGRESS/RESOLVED)
Reuse cli-agent launch controls and manage_coordination.py leases rather than reimplementing them
Event-driven, not busy-polling; idle CPU negligible and zero model calls
Hard rails: wall-clock SIGKILL, max iterations, freeze to BLOCKED_ON_HUMAN after repeated non-zero exits
No live remote writes or destructive operations in tests; Human Gate applies to state-changing dispatches
score_basis: Scores carried over from the 2026-11-02 registration (5x4)/(0.1x2)=100 and not reassessed after the 2026-11-08 refactor; treat as provisional.
